articleTitle: A switched reluctance motor drive system with voltage regulation and Power Factor Correction front-end converter
abstract: A Modified Z-Source Converter (MQZSC) is presented in this paper as a front end converter for the switched reluctance motor (SRM) drive system in order to perform voltage regulation and Power Factor Correction (PFC). In conventional SRM drive system pulsation current causes high Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) in the input source and DC link voltage cannot be controlled. In this paper using the MQZSC voltage of the DC link is regulated according to the operation mode and requirements of the drive system. Average Current Control (ACC) PFC has been integrated in to the control system of the front end converter to reduce THD and enhance the power factor. Also an angle control has been implemented in the SRM drive system to reduce the torque ripple alongside the front end controller. A software simulation has been done to verify the proposed drive system.

articleTitle: Blind consecutive extraction of multi-carrier spread spectrum data from digital images
abstract: We address blind extraction of spread spectrum data embedded in a digital image. The multicarrier iterative generalized least-squares (M-IGLS) data extraction algorithm is the basis of our study and a new algorithm based on M-IGLS is introduced in which both computational complexity and data extraction accuracy are enhanced. In the new method named multicarrier consecutive iterative generalized least-squares (M-CIGLS) algorithm, neither the cover image nor the spread spectrum carriers are required for the hidden data extraction. Additionally, knowledge of the number of carriers is no more needed. Simulation results show the ability of this method to extract data with a superior performance with respect to M-IGLS. Moreover, the probability of bit error rate is comparable with those of obtained by informed algorithms in which both cover image and spread spectrum carriers are known.

articleTitle: Synthesis and preparation of ZnO NWs for glucose biosensing
abstract: In this article the fabrication process and test results of an electrochemical glucose biosensor based on zinc oxide (ZnO) nanowires (NWs) synthesized on an interdigitated electrode (IDE) is reported. The ZnO thin films and ZnO NWs were prepared by sol-gel and hydrothermal methods, respectively. The ZnO NWs, possessing good electron transfer, have shown good performance in glucose detection especially when modified with APTES. The proposed sensor shows a low detection limit (0.03 mg/dL) of glucose with a response time of 120 seconds indicating that the device has appropriate operation and hence, can be employed in commercial setups.

articleTitle: A load and delay-aware internet of things virtual sensors service assignment in Cloud
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has gained significant importance recently, as the number of connected objects increases. The information produced by these objects can be collected to create virtual sensors. These sensors are then connected to the Internet via gateways. In this paper, we propose a multi-objective service assignment algorithm for assigning the requests of thesesensors to the gateways. This algorithm aims to minimize the mean time of sending requests to the gateways and the mean time of responding to these requests. In addition, load balance is maintained between the gateways. Our algorithm is the combination of multi-objective firefly algorithm and queue theory. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has significantly less mean response time and mean transmission time compared to Queue based Round Robin (QRR) algorithm.

articleTitle: Highly birefringent photonic crystal fiber with flattened negative dispersion over the S+C+L+U wavelength bands
abstract: A photonic crystal fiber with elliptical air holes in its center is proposed and investigated for high birefringence and flattened negative dispersion. It is shown that the proposed structure provides a dispersion of -419.5 ps/(nm.km) with a fluctuation of 9 ps/(nm.km) over the S+C+L+U wavelength bands which makes it suitable for dispersion compensation. Furthermore, it provides a high birefringence of 0.033 at the wavelength of 1.55 μm which is useful for sensor applications. The effect of fabrication tolerance on the dispersion characteristic is also reported.

articleTitle: Robust networked control of load frequency in multi-area interconnected power system
abstract: Due to deregulated power system, increasing the use of distributed generations and movement toward smart grid the use of networked control system (NCS) to support ancillary service such as automatic generation control (AGC) system is increased. However, beside the variety of advantages of NCS, using that have challenges such as fixed and random time delay. This time delay can degrade the power system dynamic performance and even cause instability. This paper investigates the delay-dependent robust stability of the AGC scheme. Since free weighting matrices are used to express this approach and since appropriate ones are selected by means of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), the proposed method is less conservative than existing ones. The proposed control structure is such that the time delay enters in controller design stages, improve robust performance in compared with other proposed controllers. Also, for one example studied, the effectiveness and offering significant improvements (against fixed and random time delay) over previous ones is shown.

articleTitle: Investigation of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs with step aluminum mole fraction and doping level in the barrier layer
abstract: Gallium-nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) with step aluminum mole fraction or doping concentration in the barrier is reported. The barrier layer is divided into two Source Side (SS) and Drain Side (DS) parts with the same lengths and thicknesses, but with different aluminum mole fraction or doping levels. Average of the aluminum mole fraction or doping concentration in the barrier is equal to those in the conventional structure. Changes that happen in the maximum lateral electric field, breakdown voltage, maximum DC trans-conductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>), drain current, gate-source capacitance, cut off frequency and DC output conductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>) as a function of different source side (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SS</inf>) and drain side (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf>) barrier doping levels or different aluminum mole fractions at source side (X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SS</inf>) and drain side (X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf>) are studied in details. Simulation results illustrate that a smaller N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> compared to N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SS</inf> improves the breakdown voltage. On the other hand, decreasing N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SS</inf> reduces the gate-source capacitance and DC output conductance. With varying N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SS</inf> and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf>, the DC trans-conductance has a nonlinear variation. Also, proposed structures with smaller X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SS</inf> than X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> reduces the maximum lateral electric field and then improve the breakdown voltage and g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>.

articleTitle: Perceptual compressive sensing based on contrast sensitivity function: Can we avoid non-visible redundancies acquisition?
abstract: Conventional compressive sensing (CS) attempts to acquire the most important part of a signal directly. In fact, CS avoids acquisition of existed statistical redundancies of a signal. Since the sensitivity of the human eye is different for each frequency, in addition to statistical redundancies, there exist perceptual redundancies in an image which human eye could not detect them. In this paper, we propose a novel CS approach in which the acquisition of non-visible information is also avoided. Hence, we could expect a better compression performance. We deploy the weighted CS idea to consider these perceptual redundancies in our model. Moreover, the block-based compressed sensing is favorable since it has some advantages: (a) It needs low memory to store the sensing matrix and sparsifying basis. (b) All blocks can be reconstructed in parallel. Therefore, we apply our proposed scheme in the block-based framework to make it practical to use. Simulation results verify the superiority of our proposed method compared to the other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: A 2.4GHz class-E power amplifier with high power control range
abstract: One of the most power consuming blocks in a transceiver is power amplifier. Power dissipation of power amplifier plays a critical role in mobile transmitters whose power supplies have been limited. In this paper, a high-power power amplifier with a high power control range is presented. The stacked topology along with a combination of two intermediate nodes matching technique are adopted to adjust the amplitude of the power amplifier voltages and eliminate their phase misalignment. As a result, the supply voltage increases, and high output power is achieved. Advanced cascode power control technique is employed to control the output power of the power amplifier and obtain optimum DC bias with a linear dynamic range of 40dB. The power amplifier which is simulated using 0.13μm CMOS technology delivers maximum output power of 26dBm at 2.4GHz frequency.

articleTitle: Finite-time fault-tolerant control for an active suspension system
abstract: In this paper, a novel finite-time fault-tolerant control law is developed to solve the stabilization control problem of an active suspension system. The requirement of prior information about the bounds of the system uncertainties and actuator faults is obviated using the parameter adaptation laws introduced in the control scheme. Furthermore, Lyapunov's stability analysis indicates that the proposed control technique can provide desirable features such as fault-tolerant capability, finite-time convergence, robustness to model uncertainties and disturbance rejection ability. Finally, the simulation comparisons between the developed control technique and the other existing controller in the literature show the improved performance of the proposed control method regarding the ride comfort and the vehicle safety.

articleTitle: Facial mark detection and removal using graph relations and statistics
abstract: Face Analysis is an important task in image processing. Most of these tasks centralized on face recognition and detection. One of different ways for deceiving automatic face analysis systems is mark notation on the skin. On the other hand some applications attempts to eliminate defects of the face. Hence, in this paper we try to detect and remove skin marks on the face, whether they're natural or not. Our algorithm passes face image through appropriate filters to get mark candidates and then create a graph space using 8-point neighborhood relations of mark candidates image pixels. Then we compute probabilities of each mark candidate using four measures based on intensity of occurrence, shape density, uniqueness in local area and color difference. Then using a threshold, we distinguish marks and false candidates. Finally we use the most similar adjacent area around mark to remove the mark from skin. Our algorithm represents significant accuracy in mole detection and removal.

articleTitle: Resonant slotted-waveguide antenna array using open-ended SIW resonator
abstract: In this paper, a new resonant slotted-waveguide antenna array based on the open-ended SIW resonator is presented. In the conventional resonant slotted-waveguide arrays an in-phase excitation is achieved by adjusting the distance between slots one half guided wavelength (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>/2) and alternating themon the opposite sides of the center line. The open-ended SIW resonator is capable of supporting infinite wavelength propagation and hence the distance between slots can be unequal with the same phases. This capability can be used for distance tapering to have low sidelobe level (SLL). A 9-element array with unequal spacing based on this kind of resonator is designed and simulated at 10 GHz. By using genetic algorithm (GA), the distances between slots is determined in order to have a low SLL. The simulation results show that the side lobe level of the designed antenna is 16 dB.

articleTitle: A robust approach to schedule flexible ramp in Real-Time Electricity Market considering Demand Response
abstract: Penetration of renewable energy resources in power systems and their uncertain natures have caused some challenges in a Real-Time Markets (RTMs) such as price forecasting and balancing issues. Independent System Operator's (ISO's) introduced flexible ramp products in RTMs to overcome this problem. In this paper, a novel method is presented for scheduling flexible ramp requirements in RTM considering Demand Response (DR). In this method, net load uncertainty is modeled using robust optimization (RO) technique in which each period is defined by some scenarios and RO is used to model the uncertainty of each scenario. In order to verify the effectiveness of the method, a typical case study is conducted and the results are compared with the deterministic and stochastic approaches. It is shown that the proposed method is capable of controlling the price spikes and load curtailments.

articleTitle: Optimum design for a hybrid system with respect to cost and reliability based on stochastic methods
abstract: In the recent years, there is a growing trend of energy consumption all over the world, and we are facing an unquenchable demand for electricity. On the other hand, international growth in natural gas price and different restrictions on emitting greenhouse gases cause increase in expenses of fossil fuels power generation. As a result, renewable energy resources especially wind and solar energies are the best alternatives for power generation. The main disadvantage of wind and solar resources is their uncertainties. Cooperation of wind and solar systems could help to overcome this problem and have a more reliable network. In this paper, uncertainty model of a sample system (consist of photovoltaic panels, wind turbines and battery) is drawn out by probability and statistics calculations. Furthermore, a standalone microgrid is organized and designed with respect to the expected energy not supplied (EENS) and system cost indicators by using Monte Carlo method.

articleTitle: Extended LT decoder based on extra ripples
abstract: The ripple that was introduced to the decoder of LT codes plays a key role in the decoding process. Even Luby's degree distributions are defined so that this ripple maintains a reasonable size. For low block length which have many application in wireless, LT codes doesn't work properly so in this paper to extend the decodability of the LT codes for low block lengths, extra ripples are introduced to the decoder. Retaining the LT decoder's simplicity, it is possible to regenerate the main ripple and extend the decoding by means of these extra ripples. As the simulation and analytical results based on recursion of probability distributions show, lower error probabilities can be achieved. For the new decoder even the operational complexity is not increased that much due to the structure of LT codes. Even lower complexities in term of XOR operations can be achieved as the complexity of LT codes is mainly related to the number of edges in the decoding graph.

articleTitle: Motion segmentation with hand held cameras using structure from motion
abstract: Motion detection and segmentation are used in many applications of computer vision. The goal of this segmentation is to extract moving object from its background. This segmentation would be more challengeable when the camera is moving itself. This paper considers the addressing of this problem using structure from motion (SFM) techniques. First, using the RANSAC algorithm the Epipolar geometry between two-view images is estimated to calculate the fundamental matrix. Second, the dense optical flow is used to find the corresponding point for all the pixels. Then the corresponding points which do not lie on their Epipolar lines are detected. These points will introduce the moving objects. The experiments show the performance of our algorithm in real scene.

articleTitle: Energy efficient resource allocation in two-tier heterogeneous network with inband full-duplex communications
abstract: In this paper we investigate energy-efficient resource allocation in a two-tier orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) network with inband full-duplex communications. The base station (BS) assignment, subcarrier and power allocation policies are jointly considered to optimize system's energy efficiency (EE) and to satisfy users' quality of service (QoS) in both uplink and downlink. We formulate the energy efficient resource allocation as a mixed integer and non-convex optimization problem which is generally hard to solve. To deal with this complexity, we first propose two heuristic algorithms for BS assignment and subcarrier allocation, then we transform the main power allocation problem into an equivalent convex one, and address it by Lagrangian dual decomposition method. Simulation results show that our proposed algorithm can considerably increase system's EE as compared to the existing works.

articleTitle: A transmit diversity technique for space shift keying modulation
abstract: Space shift keying (SSK) modulation is a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technique in which antenna indices are used for sending information bits. Eliminating inter channel interference (ICI) and increasing of spectral efficiency without increasing the bandwidth requirements are among the advantages of this technique. However, this modulation did not exploit transmit diversity. To deal with this problem, an antenna selection algorithm is introduced in this paper. Transmit antennas are divided into K groups with the same number of antennas. The receiver selects one group in each transmission block according to CSI. If this group satisfies a special criterion introduced in this paper, the receiver sends the group index to the transmitter through feedback to be used for sending information. Otherwise, no group will send information bits. We have analyzed Average Bit Error Rate (ABER) performance of the system for a special case of two antennas in each group. Simulation results show diversity order improvement for our proposed scheme in comparison to conventional SSK system. Moreover, a precise matching can be seen between our analysis and simulations.

articleTitle: An artificial neural network based on Izhikevich neuron model
abstract: In the recent years, artificial neural network have been used to improvement of system identification. The performance of neural network directly depends on the hidden layer, which include weights and activation functions of the network. In addition Genetic Algorithms are used to learn of neural network as a type of evolutionary computing algorithms. In this paper, the structure of hidden layers and weights are modified by using biological neuron model of Izhikevich. These two methods, Genetic Algorithms and biological model of neuron, merge together for designing a novel structure.

articleTitle: Persian large vocabulary name recognition system (FarsName)
abstract: There has been no isolated word recognition database for the Persian language so far. In this paper we introduce FarsName dataset which contains 20 thousands isolated-word Persian utterances spoken by 226 speakers from all regions of the country each saying an average of 88 Persian names. There is a total of 5235 unique names in this dataset. Various cell phone brands have been used to record this dataset. This indicates the high diversity of the utterances in this dataset. We have been able to achieve 10.34% WER on this set using Kaldi. This is a very good performance considering the recording environment have been normal and potentially noisy.

articleTitle: Hybrid processing for multi-pair massive MIMO two-way relay network
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology in combination with cooperative communications is an emerging paradigm which adds advantages of high spectral efficiency and diversity gains to extended coverage and increased network capacity of relay systems. However, the implementation cost and hardware complexity is limiting factor imposed by large number of required radio frequency (RF) chains. The hybrid processing with a far reduced number of RF chains is a solution being performed in analog and low-dimensional digital domains. In this paper, we consider a multi-pair two-way relay system where the relay node equipped with large-scale antennas assists to exchange information between single-antenna users. We propose low complexity three stages hybrid beamforming techniques based on linear baseband processing zero-forcing reception/transmission (ZFR/ZFT) and maximum ratio combining/transmission (MRC/MRT) schemes by applying phase controls in reception and transmission stages and performing low-dimensional digital beamforming in the middle stage. Our simulation results show performance of proposed hybrid processing techniques and corresponding full digital processing methods are close together.

articleTitle: Bus measurements protection against bad data injection in electric power grids
abstract: System security indices play a crucial role with regard to monitoring system statues. These indices are derived from system measurements which are prone to either intentional or unintentional noises. To alleviate the effect of intentional noises, it is required to protect measurements data from bad data injection. In this regard, this paper intends to propose an approach to determine priority order of protected bus measurements in order to negate the effects of bad data injection on security indices. With this in mind, two security severity indices, the over loading risk index and the under voltage risk index, are considered. Genetic algorithm serves to find the highest deteriorating effect of bad data injection on security indices. The effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method is examined through applying it to the standard IEEE 30-bus system. The obtained results emphasize the importance of protecting bus measurements against bad data injection.

articleTitle: A tunable-Q 4-path bandpass filter with Gm-C second-order baseband impedances
abstract: An active switched-capacitor 4-path bandpass filter suitable for multi-standard applications in ultra-high frequency (UHF) band with different channel bandwidths is designed and simulated in 0.18 µm CMOS technology. The baseband impedance of the filter is implemented as a second-order G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>-C low-pass filter which can be used to tune the channel bandwidth as well as the quality factor (Q) of the RF filter. The center frequency of the filter can be tuned from 100 MHz up to 1.5 GHz by changing the clock frequency applied to the filter while its bandwidth can be tuned by tuning impedance parameters in any center frequency. To do so, the baseband impedance utilizes a frequency dependent negative resistor (i.e. FDNR) structure for having a second-order impedance. The proposed filter achieves 12–40 MHz channel bandwidth, about 2 dB noise figure (NF), and 12 dB rejection at 1GHz center frequency. According to the post-layout simulation results, the power consumption of the filter is 14 mW at 1.8 volts supply voltage consuming only 0.04 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> silicon area.

articleTitle: Design and investigation of an elliptic micro-ring resonator slow light device
abstract: Ring resonators can be readily integrated in array geometries. It is nonlinear phase response produces particular intensity output function. Fast and slow light can simultaneously be achieved by polarization birefringence. In this paper, we've proposed an elliptic microring structure coupled to a waveguide with Silicon on Isolator (SOI) technology. The results show that with this structure we can increase group delay. In addition number of microring resonators affect group delay and bandwidth. To the best of our knowledge, for eccentricity 0.3, we've obtained Slow Down Factor (SDF) about 100 which has considerable increase in comparison with circular one. We simulate magnitude and phase response for θ = 30° that is the angle between resonating polarization of elliptic shape and degenerate straight waveguide. Also group delay and SDF for different eccentricity have been calculated.

articleTitle: A low noise and high gain distributed amplifier for ku band in 180nm CMOS
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a 4-stage CMOS 12– 18 GHZ distributed amplifier where each stage is a cascaded two-stage topology. We incorporate the idea of replacing the termination impedance with short circuits in both gate and drain terminations to achieve a band-pass frequency response. Using the cascaded two-stage amplifier, we achieve a reasonable gain-bandwidth performance and a smooth transfer function. For the proposed topology, we derive design formulas for low and high cutoff frequencies, input/output impedance matching, and voltage gain. Since the gate termination impedance, as a significant noise source, is replaced with short circuit in the gate line, we achieve a noise figure lower than 4 dB. The proposed amplifier provides a gain of 25 dB while consumes 40 mW from a 1.8 V supply. Our simulation results show that S11 is below −10.2 dB and S22 is below −11.4 dB.

articleTitle: Design optimal velocity profile for energy saving in metro system using classical optimization method
abstract: In recent decades, by rapid development of industry and urbanization, the energy crisis, environmental pollution and traffic congestion, the railway transportation is the main transportation form and it will be more attractive in the future. In this way, optimal energy consumption play an important role in the railway transportation. In this paper, a new strategy for designing the online optimal speed profile based the mathematical classic methods, is presented. In this strategy, there are different modes, such as maximum power, maximum braking, hold speed and coasting, during a trip between two stations are considered. Based on the know information about operating modes, gradient of track and speed limits of track and train an optimization energy consumption is expressed to find the optimal switching points between the modes. By using the known information of Tehran metro line 5 and designing the speed profile for this line, simulation results in the Matlab software are shown.

articleTitle: Power quality enhancement in islanded microgrid
abstract: In recent years, the penetration of distribution generations (DGs) has increased. Also the role of distributed generation has significantly increased not only as power generator, but also as an important factor in power quality improvement. In this paper, a method is proposed for reducing the voltage unbalance while the DG is not connected to the grid. Control loops pertaining to voltage and frequency powers are provided in order to control the voltage and frequency of local load. Besides, the virtual impedance loop and proportional-resonant controller are also utilized in the control loop. The simulation results confirm the functionality of the control strategy and the controllers in eliminating the imbalance.

articleTitle: A novel method for throughput analysis of MAC protocols in Multi-user MIMO networks
abstract: Throughput inefficiency of CSMA/CA MAC protocol enforces to think about designing new MACs with higher throughputs. Multi-User MAC protocols are among those MAC protocols which are designed to handle multiple simultaneous data transmissions and provide higher throughputs in data networks. In this paper, we are going to propose a novel method for throughput analysis of such protocols based on physical parameters of the antennas in both the receiver and the transmitter sides. In order to validate our approach, first we present a simple MAC protocol which handles two simultaneous data transmissions in the uplink of a Multi-user MIMO network. Then, we apply our method on the presented MAC and obtain the throughput of the network. Finally, we validate our method with simulation results.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient and delay aware power control in interference wireless networks
abstract: Designing energy efficient delay aware communication networks become an inevitable trend due to change of data traffic types. In this paper, we present an energy efficient and delay aware competitive power control in interference limited wireless networks. To achieve this goal, the utility function is defined as the ratio of effective capacity to power consumption which is termed Effective Energy Efficiency (EEE). Then, a non-cooperative game for power control algorithm is proposed. It is shown that the considered power control admits a Nash equilibrium (NE) which is guaranteed to be unique. Our analytical results show that NE has the same structure of spectral efficient design but with a different threshold. Furthermore, our simulation results show that our energy efficient game achieves EEE gains relative to spectral efficient game.

articleTitle: Study on Shunt reactor energization effects on power transformers
abstract: A Shunt reactor energization produces a decayed direct current in the network leading to phenomena which some of them are currently high-interest topics in the power system study. One of these phenomena is the DC bias in the magnetic core flux of the power transformer. This phenomenon caused some problem in the 400/132/20 kV transformer of the Golfaraj substation at the commissioning phase leading to the current research to find out the problem and its solution. This research investigates the effect of the shunt reactor energization on the power transformers using the PSCAD/EMTDC software to understand the phenomena better. In this paper, first of all, the phenomenon mechanism is explained in detail using a simple network, then, the different parameters affecting this phenomenon are studied like the effect of the line parameters, the transformer connections and etc.

articleTitle: A novel remote tunable maximum power point tracking controller implementation for photovoltaic systems
abstract: Nowadays many studies have been done on renewable energies to overcome many difficulties of traditional energy consumption. Various kinds of renewable energy sources are available. One of the attractive fields for renewable energy researchers is photovoltaic (PV) systems. To ensure high efficiency of a PV system, numerous algorithms have been developed as maximum power point tracking (MPPT). This paper introduces a novel remote tunable maximum power point tracking (RTMPPT) controller implementation for photovoltaic systems. PV sites' controller which could be located in various regions can be managed or changed by a remote controller site using RTMPPT. The controller site is connected to all PV sites using a typical local area network (LAN) or the Internet. Since RTMPPT periodically updates the controller algorithm of each PV site, the effects of climate changes or seasonal temperature variation will be considered in the controller. Hence the controller is adaptive to variation of temperature and/or irradiation ensuring high efficiency in different climates.

Author Keywords: Remote Tunable Maximum Power Point Tracking

articleTitle: Design of adaptive proportional-integral-weighted (PIw) controllers for control of a class of nonlinear uncertain systems
abstract: Study on the potential abilities of the proportional-integral-weighted (PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sup>) controllers, as a recently proposed generalization for proportional-integral (PI) controllers, can be useful for improving the performance of traditional control systems. In this paper, adaptive PI and adaptive PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sup> controllers are designed to be used in control of a special class of nonlinear uncertain systems based on the Lyapanuv stability theorem. The effectiveness of the proposed controllers is illustrated by applying the proposed schemes to a Continuous Stirred-Tank Reactor (CSTR) system with an unknown parameter. Simulation results indicate that using adaptive PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sup> controllers, in comparison to using the adaptive PI controller, can improve the performance of the control system.

articleTitle: Correction of timing skew error in TIADC's using second generation wavelets
abstract: This paper presents a simple algorithm for correcting the timing skew errors in time-interleaved ADC's that are necessary to electronically realize the software defined radio (SDR). To compensate the timing skew of non-evenly sampled data in the output of a TIADC, we exploited the lifting scheme implementing three-point median interpolation wavelet. Based on that second-generation wavelet, the TIADC output is decomposed into detail and approximation components namely, difference and average. Then, the timing errors are canceled out from the detail component by thresholding procedure. The method is easily implementable and reversible without any need to memory hardware for realizing practical SDR systems. Simulations show that the proposed method improves the SFDR and SNR after denoising to 11.14 dB and 0.0009 dB respectively. SNR can even be more fully improved by structural optimization.

articleTitle: A new islanding scheme based on multi-objective optimization for distribution systems implemented with DGs
abstract: The successive occurrence of events and blackouts is one of the most important threats for the security of power systems. The structure of network being divided into several parts and creation of unwanted islands are the most important behavioral features of a power system during the process of forming blackouts. One of the appropriate approaches for increasing the security of power systems in this field is to divide the power system into proper islands in an intentional and controllable way. In today's power systems where distributed generation units are increasingly used, these units could have a positive effect on the creation of independent islands during successive events. In this paper, a new approach based on multi-objective non-dominated sorting particle swarm optimization (NSPSO) algorithm is presented for optimal determination of boundaries of intentional islands in distribution systems in presence of distributed generation resources in order to decrease load interruption and system losses. The proposed approach is applied on the modified IEEE 33-bus distribution system and the optimal boundaries of intentional islands are determined in this system. The results show the high accuracy of proposed model in intentional islanding.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of surface curvature from the triangular flat meshes for the calculation radar cross section of electrically large objects
abstract: In physical optics prediction of radar cross section, the surface of the object is usually modeled by flat triangular meshes in order to simplify the intersection test and electromagnetic field calculations. This geometrical representation ignores the surface curvature and the resulting changes in the curvature of the reflected wavefront. As a result the accuracy of radar cross section prediction decreases. This paper uses a bilinear approximation method to estimate the normal vector variations of surface and then uses the curvature tensor to recover the surface curvature data from flat meshes. Numerical results show that the presented method properly recovers the surface curvature at a low computational cost. By using the recovered curvature data in physical optics calculations, the accuracy of radar cross section prediction of a missile model is enhanced 1dB on average.

articleTitle: Closed form formula for longitudinal slot of LWAs with minimum side lobe level
abstract: In this paper a closed-form expression is introduced to calculate slot shape of long slot leaky wave waveguide antennas at its fundamental mode of operation with minimum side lobe level (SLL). The derived equation is a function of geometrical parameters of the structure. This is an advantage because they show a clear relationship between geometrical parameters of the antenna and radiated field that allows intelligent modification of the pattern. The Gaussian slot is used to obtain the best radiation pattern with lowest SLL. The results obtained by introduced formula are compared with the full wave commercial simulator such as HFSS software which confirms the accuracy of the introduced equations.

articleTitle: Robust texture image retrieval based on two dimensional cyclic spectral analysis
abstract: This paper, presents a new feature generation algorithm for texture image retrieval. The spectral correlation function (SCF) is expanded into two dimensions and then a new efficient algorithm in order to estimate two-dimensional spectral correlation function (2D_SCF) is proposed. The proposed algorithm reveals hidden periodicity of texture and by considering the local information between pixels of texture image generates noise resistant and efficient features. Since the proposed algorithm produces many 2D_SCF coefficients, three statistical features are selected to describe these coefficients. Therefore, the extracted features at different regions of bi_frequency of 2D_SCF planes are utilized to retrieve the texture images. This study shows that the new algorithm has high performance in retrieval of Brodatz texture images. Experimental results show that the presented method increases retrieval accuracy with and without noise in comparing with other studies in this area.

articleTitle: Joint channel assignment and routing in Software Defined wireless mesh networks
abstract: Interference among wireless links is the main reason for capacity reduction in wireless mesh networks. Allowing multiple radio interface use in a mesh router with different frequency channel is often presented as a possible way to improve the network capacity. One efficient way is using a centralized controller to assign proper frequency channel to radio interfaces which would significantly reduce the interference. Furthermore, proposing a routing protocol which consider interference as a leading factor for finding a path can noticeably increase the overall throughput. Since Software-Defined Networking provide more flexible and manageable networks by decoupling between control plane and data plane and implementing the control and management in a logically centralized controller, it can be a good choice. This paper is supposed to use a controller in a SDN wireless mesh networks to assign channels based on a static channel assignment algorithm and making routing decision based on the remained interference between links.

articleTitle: Multi-channel ZnO nanowire FET performance: Utilizing different gate materials
abstract: In this paper, the effect of different gate materials, including Metal, p-type and n-type silicon, on electrical characteristics of zinc oxide nanowire field effect transistors (FETs) is studied with TCAD software. To analyze the ZnO NWFET performance, I-V characteristic, electron mobility and threshold voltage are investigated and compared. Comparing results indicates, p-type silicon gate ZnO NWFET has proper output performance with a threshold voltage of 0.75V, on/off current ratio of ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> and electron mobility of ~96 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/V. s in the transistor channel. This device is then used for multi-channel FETs in order to raise FETs drain current. Simulation results show the current is multiplied by six in using three channel FET. This device can be used for applications which need a high current response and high current on/off ratio.

articleTitle: A hybrid control strategy for stable operation of converter-based DG resources in distribution grids with shunt active power filter capability
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid control strategy for integration of distributed generations (DGs) to distribution grids using power converters is suggested. The fuzzy tracking control based on Lyapunov function is presented for the current loop of the interfaced converter to overcome the problems of conventional control methods. The proposed control plan guarantees the system stability, appropriate tracking of the reference currents and gives a proper transient waveform. By means of the proposed control plan, the grid-interfacing converter will be utilized as: (1) power converter to inject the active power extracted from DGs to the grid, and (2) shunt active power filter (SAPF) to provide the reactive, harmonic, neutral and unbalanced currents of the grid-connected loads with a quick dynamic response. The simulation results, carried out through MATLAB/Simulink software, demonstrate the suitable operation of the suggested control plan.

articleTitle: Investigation of effective connectivity alteration during hypnosis induction using direct directed transfer function
abstract: Hypnosis therapy is a widely applied method for treating psychiatric disorders, pain relief, and sleep irregularity. Research findings have demonstrated that hypnosis therapy will be useful, mostly for high hypnotizable subjects. Another factor which makes hypnosis therapy efficient is the hypnotic depth. In this study, we were interested in relationship between hypnotic depth and its corresponding effective connectivity patterns. Furthermore, effective connectivity changes between different hypnotizable subjects was studied. Direct directed transfer function (dDTF) was used in order to estimate effective connectivity between EEG channels. Based on our result, in medium and high hypnotizable groups, as subjects reach to their final depth of hypnosis, effective connectivity patterns were significantly reduced in delta and theta frequency bands while for low hypnotizable group, reduction was only seen in delta band and effective connectivity among channels in theta, beta and gamma frequency bands remained unchanged.

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation of 20 kW solar power station in grid-connected mode (a case study)
abstract: In this paper, the reliability of a sample solar plant is investigated because of plying an essential role in consent of different stakeholders in connection to national electricity network. Continuous-time Markov chain method is selected as computational method in this paper and also because of the increasing importance of reliability studies in power systems and existence of an integrated and unified structure in performing these studies, data processing and collection system in Iran's national electricity network that has an essential role in reliability studies is shown. Since production sector and distribution sector power systems are different for investigating reliability evaluation and performance, their reliability indicators are separately presented.

articleTitle: Source current reconstruction method and field transformation with LSMR iterative solver
abstract: The source current reconstruction method (SRM) is based on the equivalent principle in which the equivalent current of the antenna under test (AUT) is reconstructed from the known electric field and can be used for both field transformation and antenna diagnostic applications. In this method, the equivalent currents at the AUT aperture are discretized based on the known basis functions and then these currents are determined with the inverse method of moments (MoM) techniques. The large matrix equation that is created by the SRM is conventionally solved by different types of conjugate gradient (CG) solver. In this paper, a recently proposed least square iterative solver, LSMR, is used as a SRM matrix solver. Results of current reconstruction and field transformation with LSMR are reported in the paper and compared with the conjugate gradient solver. It is shown that in the presence of white Gaussian noise with different SNR, LSMR iterative solver is more stable and can reconstruct the equivalent currents sooner and better than the conventional CG solver.

articleTitle: An optimized dechirping approach for moving target velocity estimation by synthetic aperture radar
abstract: In this paper, a novel algorithm for motion parameters estimation, i.e. radial and along-track velocities, of ground-moving targets by synthetic aperture radar is proposed. This algorithm transforms the conventional two-dimensional search operation into an efficient one-dimensional search operation. Thus, a significant reduction in computational load is achieved. After clutter suppression by traditional methods like Displaced Phase Center Antenna (DPCA), the remaining echoes, which belong to the moving target, represent a chirp-like behavior. Two important parameters of this inherent LFM signal, i.e. Doppler centroid frequency and Doppler rate, are estimated in an one-dimensional optimization problem of a deramping approach. These two parameters are of vital importance for image formation algorithms. Because the suitable matched filter in the azimuth compression part should be designed based on them. Performance evaluation is done by computer simulations to validate the theoretical discussions.

articleTitle: Power allocation for Cognitive Radio MIMO-OFDM broadcast channels based on block-diagonalization beamforming
abstract: In this paper, the beamforming design and power allocation problem for MIMO-OFDM cognitive radio broadcast channel is investigated. Due to the non-convexity of this problem, the Block Diagonalization is proposed as beamforming strategy which converts the problem to only a power allocation problem. The power allocation problem is solved based on the standard convex optimization framework, and iterative algorithms with a closed form power allocation are proposed to search optimal dual variables based on KKT conditions. As a comparison, suboptimal solutions with lower complexity are proposed based on resolving combinatorial constraints to individual constraints. Simulation results validate proposed algorithms and evaluate their performance over various scenarios.

articleTitle: A perturbation-approach error model derivation of local-level gimbaled INS to determine its oscillatory modes analytically
abstract: Error analysis of INS systems is a crucial issue in navigation problems. In this paper, the gimbaled INS is modeled, its navigation equations are written in the local level (navigation) frame, its analytic error model is derived using perturbation approach and its eigenvalues are calculated for the case of a stationary host vehicle to determine its oscillatory modes. The analytic resulted are verified by simulating the local-level gimbaled INS mechanization equations with noisy inputs and also by running Monte Carlo simulation showing that the analytically-derived oscillatory modes are apparent in simulation results.

articleTitle: A fast scheme for TD-MoM analysis of PEC surfaces in free space
abstract: A new scheme to solve the potential integrals of time domain integral equation (TDIE) for planar PEC scatterers in free space is presented. In this method self-term singularities of the potential integrals are numerically calculated. The method uses some selected points in the source and observation patches in TD-MoM solver to calculate the potential integrals. The numerical integration of the potential integrals is almost two times faster than other methods that extracted or canceled singularity of self-terms. Numerical results illustrate the accuracy and simulation time of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Armchair graphene nanoribbons: A synthesis precision study
abstract: In recent years we have witnessed many breakthroughs in the field of graphene nanoribbons. The promising features of these structures have created new opportunities in manufacturing electronic devices. However, due to the low precision of synthesizing procedures, process variation is still as a concerning challenge in developing nanoscale devices. In this paper, we have theoretically studied the impact of process variation during the progress of Boron/Nitrogen doping, strain implement, and antidote insertion. Our study will focus on Armchair Graphene Nanoribbons. In order to investigate our results, simulations using the MATLAB tool, tight-binding approach, and Monte Carlo method have been carried out. Our results demonstrated that the vertical doping method is the most reliable approach in compare to others. This approach also provides tunable band gap size in a wide range, allowing its usage in future nanoscale devices.

articleTitle: Modeling and verifying timed event-based systems
abstract: A part of large scale distributed and heterogeneous systems are event-based in which temporal properties play a critical role. In this paper, considering the temporal properties we first present a semi-formal based specification model using UML statecharts and then address the conversion of this model to formal one called timed automata. Next, we deal with verification of properties stated in Timed Computation Tree Logic (TCTL) formulas in the automata. By proposing a case study, we show the application of our method.

articleTitle: Synthesis of distributed sampled-data fuzzy controller for a class of hyperbolic PDE systems
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of designing sampled-data fuzzy controller for a class of nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equation (PDE) systems. By using the sector nonlinearity approach, the exact Takagi-Sugeno (TS) hyperbolic PDE fuzzy model will be obtained. Then, based on the spatially distributed parallel distributed compensation (SDPDC), the closed-loop system will be achieved via an input delay approach. Then, based on the proposed spatially distributed Lyapunov Krasovskii functional (LKF) and also introducing some new null terms, the sufficient stability conditions will be calculated in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Finally, the proposed approach is applied to non-isothermal Plug flow reactor (PFR) to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Performance investigation of double gate junctionless pMOSFET with asymmetric doping profile for biosensing applications
abstract: In this paper, the potential capability of a novel dielectric modulated p-type junctionless MOSFET as a highly sensitive biosensor is demonstrated. A cavity is embedded in the gate insulator region for immobilizing the biomolecules. Absorption of biomolecules in the nanogap changes the gate coupling over the channel and results in the threshold voltage variation. An asymmetric doping profile is introduced in which the channel doing concentration is lower than the related source/drain values for designing a highly responsive biosensor with low static power consumption. Simulation results reveal that by considering maximum length for the nanogap and occupation of the entire volume of cavity, a maximum degree of sensitivity for the biosensor can be achieved. The results of this paper facilitate the integration of biodetection techniques with the existing CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Rigorous characteristics of dual-material gate nanoscale S-FED
abstract: Nanoscale side-contacted field effect diode (S-FED) has been introduced to realize high frequency and low power consumption in the realm of the logic gates. Two gates on the channel in S-FED structure make it possible to apply different work functions into the gates. Different gate work functions lead to unbalance carrier concentrations into the channel due to the band bending just beneath the gates. This condition complies with S-FED operation modes. Accurate investigations show drive current increases due to the appropriate carrier accumulation under the gates, therefore, using a single device with large drive current make it applicable to design high frequency and low power consumption logic circuit.

articleTitle: A high-performance LC-VCO based adaptive bandwidth, adaptive jitter phase locked loop
abstract: A new adaptive bandwidth adaptive jitter phase locked loop (PLL) is proposed and simulated. This circuit maintains an almost fixed bandwidth to reference frequency ratio and hence, jitter performance is kept unchanged. The main idea is to change the charge pump output current with the control voltage of the voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO). The idea is examined in Matlab Simulink and to implement this idea some new building blocks are proposed. Using these new building blocks, the circuit is simulated in 0.18µm CMOS technology and results are reported.

articleTitle: Spike sorting: Which clustering method should be chosen? Which circumstances affect this selection?
abstract: There have been several researches on spike sorting, the process of detection, feature extraction and clustering neural signals generated by brain neurons. How accurate spike sorting is performed, determines how much the results are reliable. Therefore, selecting among several proposed methods for each spike sorting step is a very important task. In this paper, we want to answer this question for the clustering step. We used the most common feature extraction method, i.e. PCA and the first two principal components as features. In order to have fair judgment, 3 datasets with different noise levels were used. We compared some of the most popular methods, selecting between: model-based/non model-based, simple mixtures/Dirichlet process mixtures, Normal/t-distributions for observations, Bayesian/EM clustering. Eventually, some direct and some situation-based conclusions were obtained.

articleTitle: High-gain sliding mode observers for a class of nonlinear uncertain delay systems
abstract: This paper proposes an observer for the class of triangular nonlinear systems including the model uncertainty, with constant delays in the state and input equations. It is assumed that the nonlinear perturbations satisfy the Lipschitz condition and the uncertain part is bounded. The main idea is based on the designing a high-gain observer in combination with the sliding mode observer which leads to a robust high-gain observer that has not been sufficiently studied previously. A compensation term is included in the observer dynamics that is designed based on the solution of a Lyapunov inequality. For stability analysis, if the matching condition is satisfied, by using a suitable Lyapunov-Krasovski functional, simple sufficient conditions are provided that guarantees the observation error converges to the origin asymptotically. The simulation results for a nonlinear system in triangular form illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Refocusing through cinder block walls
abstract: Through-wall imaging using a standard back projection technique is studied by employing ultra-wideband system operating over a frequency band of 1 - 3GHz. The propagation through a cinder block wall, while a circular conducting cylinder is placed behind the wall, is simulated with our analytic formulation. Effects of the cinder block wall on the target-image distortions is demonstrated. It is shown that by using the phase of Greens function of the structure, the effect of the wall can be suppressed and the target image can be refocused, provided that the wall parameters are known. Furthermore, it is shown that we can simulate direct cinder block wall reflection by using our developed analytic formulation.

articleTitle: Robust H∞ dynamic output feedback controller design for industrial boilers via LMI technique
abstract: Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) terms can be used to formulated a number of linear control problems. In this paper the robust H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> dynamic output feedback controller via LMI approach, studied for an industrial boiler-turbine unit. Boilers are essential component in the most coil fired power plant and generate steam continuously. A third order nonlinear Astrom and Bell model is considered. The boiler's output variables are drum pressure, electric power and drum water level deviation. Because of many safety factors, the outputs should be controlled. By using the advantage of LMI, one of the seventh operation points is chosen and the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> dynamic output feedback controller designed. The main goal of the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> controller is to get a good performance such as tracking performance and disturbance rejection. To achieve a good and fast response, the pole placement technique is used. According to the simulation results, the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> controller leads to good robustness and tracking response.

articleTitle: A miniaturized Artificial Magnetic Conductor using combination of ML and IDC methods
abstract: In this paper a new ML and IDC combined type of miniaturized Artificial Magnetic Conductor is proposed. The presented simulated reflection phase shows that this metasurface has a cell periodicity of 0.07λ and an in-phase bandwidth of 6.8% at 2.4 GHz resonance frequency. The measurement results validate that the structure functions approximately with preceding characteristics.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magneto-hydro-dynamics thruster with linear and helical channel
abstract: In this research, we analyze the linear and helical channels for Magneto-hydro-dynamics (MHD) thrusters. The performance characteristics of linear and helical MHD thrusters are studied with a simplified analytical model. The Magneto-hydro-dynamic problem is solved by solving the Navier-Stokes equations and electromagnetic equations, The 3D COMSOL finite element solver is employed. Physics interfaces from the AC/DC and CFD Modules of the 3D COMSOL Finite Element solver are coupled.

articleTitle: Resonant modes of asymmetric quasi-photonic crystal filters
abstract: In this article, we present an approach to manage the resonant modes in quasi-photonic crystals with five silver nanorods as its unit-cell, embedded in air. We use symmetric and asymmetric Ag nanorods. A simple electromagnetic field model is suggested to shift resonance frequencies to desirable place in spectrum, by varying the nanorods radius. This modal description lead us to achieve efficient single-band filter.

articleTitle: 7 µm-long all-optical 1×2 switch utilizing Si/VO2 hybrid waveguide
abstract: In this paper, a compact and CMOS compatible all-optical 1×2 switch based on directional coupler is proposed. One waveguide of directional coupler is a conventional silicon waveguide while else is a hybrid silicon/VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> waveguide. By optically changing the phase of VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer from insulating to metallic, dependent on VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> thickness, a great effective refractive index modification of hybrid waveguide can be reached. The significant modifications in refractive index lead to a small length required to apply a phase shift of 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</sub> in order to achieve switching mechanism. Our simulations result show that an extinction ratio and crosstalk of higher than 11 dB along only 7 μm length of switch is obtainable.

articleTitle: Design of an adjustable active CMOS true time delay circuit for wideband beamforming applications
abstract: A Ka-band true time delay circuit has been realized in 0.18 μm CMOS which incorporates a new technique for providing variable delay for broadband operation. Precise delay variation capability is obtained by introducing a tunable active inductance structure. Changing the inductance value of the proposed active inductor is achieved through enabling and disabling auxiliary transistors in the structure. The relative delay resolution and maximum delay of the implemented circuit are 520 fsec and 1.56 psec, respectively. These values correspond to the performance of a 6-bit phase shifter with phase shift step of 5.625° at a center frequency of 30 GHz. Establishing linear phase shift and accurate fine delay tuning with the proposed active inductor has resulted in 80 fsec maximum delay variation and less than 30 fsec average error over the intended frequency span of 26.5-35 GHz. The finalized circuit occupies less than 0.03 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and is associated with an insertion loss of about 8 dB with a variation of 1 dB per state.

articleTitle: Comprehensive evaluation of Transmission Company considering both value based and market based objectives
abstract: This paper proposes a comprehensive criterion for transmission network evaluation in power market. This criterion considers market objectives to maximize the Social Welfare. Also Reference Transmission Network (RTN) is observed for evaluation of Transmission Company (TransCo) optimality in power market. TransCo inherently is a company which is engaged with long-term planning, hence evaluation of this company requires long-term criterion. We modify RTN, to be a long-term criterion to evaluate TransCo in power market and so by applying fair evaluation, cost allocation faces more fairness.

articleTitle: Strain-based temperature compensation proposal for ZDSF
abstract: In this article, a temperature compensation system based on tensile strain induction is proposed. This method is applicable in zero-dispersion shifted optical fiber (ZDSF) and dispersion flattened optical fiber (DFF). In order for assessment of the operation of the proposed technique for compensation, the single-mode step index ZDSF is designed. The broadening factor is minimized at the wavelength of 1.55µm so as to adjust the zero-dispersion wavelength (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ZD</inf>). The simulation results admit that the dispersion and its slope at 1.55µm are 0.0028ps/km/nm and 0.070ps/km/nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. This dispersion slope results in the bit rate of 110 GB/s in the 100km distance at λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ZD</inf>. Furthermore, the effect of temperature variation and applied external tensile strain on its characteristics are investigated. Through the employment of tensile strain as a compensator, the effective refractive index (n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>) profile versus wavelength is preserved in λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ZD</inf> as well as all communication bands. The result is thermal impact removal from parameters such as dispersion and zero-dispersion wavelength.

articleTitle: Assessing the influence of functional connectivity estimation methods on graph metrics in resting-state fMRI
abstract: Investigations of brain functional connectivity (FC) using resting state fMRI, have recently taken much interest. Various methods have been suggested for estimation of functional relationship between anatomical brain regions. Among the model based proposed methods, correlation and coherency algorithms are more commonly used. However; the stability of these methods in calculation of brain network's metrics has not been investigated. In this study, using graph theory analysis, we examined the stability of these two algorithms using small worldness indexes and variations of graph characteristics of networks. Our findings suggested that both algorithms resulted in similar properties of brain networks which is confirmed the usability of both methods in functional connectivity studies. However correlation algorithm has lower computational complexity.

articleTitle: Design of 8 bit, 1633µm2, 444µW squarer hardware for high performance VLSI applications
abstract: In this paper, a new scheme for design and VLSI implementation of squarer circuits is proposed. The proposed design is based on further analysis and modification of squaring function's mathematical expression and provides high efficiency in hardware implementation. This improvement is based on two techniques, first, algebraic rearrangement of each result bit, and second, using anticipated symmetry from previously calculated results and applying it for other parts of the circuit. The proposed squarer has been implemented in TSMC 180nm CMOS technology and evaluation results demonstrates 14 percent reduction in die area, 18 percent reduction in static power consumption and also minor improvement in performance compared to conventional squarer.

articleTitle: Interference alignment in the multi input multi output cellular network systems with incomplete measurement of channel information
abstract: This paper explores the problem of interference alignment (IA) in cellular multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) cellular network systems with incomplete channel information. With regards to the realization of the cellular networks, incomplete channel information obtained from the channel is an important part. As to the significance of the issue, the IA with the accessibility of incomplete channel information on both sides of the receiver and transmitter channels is explored. Consequently, performance criteria such as the rate of inadequate channel are obtained. Finally, by providing simulation, verification issues are expressed in different conditions.

articleTitle: Tunable sorting of micro- and nano-particles in a microfluidic system using near-field optics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new structure that can trap and sort particles with size of micro and nanometers. To investigate its operating principles we calculate the optical forces exerted on a particle using Maxwell's stress tensor. The optical forces are originating from interaction between the particle and the propagating surface plasmons polaritons excited on gold stripes. We evaluate polystyrene sphere radius for which the potential depth reaches its threshold value of 10 k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>T. The potential depth is computed from the lateral component of optical force (F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>) for three stripes with widths of 1, 2 and 3μm. It is shown that this structure can sort polystyrene particles in four ranges with different radii. The boundaries of the ranges are 1010, 490 and 280nm. As advantage of this method, it can be tuned with changing illumination power or stripes widths that can be used for biological optical sorting.

articleTitle: Low voltage hybrid plasmonic-organic phase modulator
abstract: In this article, design and simulation of a novel low voltage phase modulator is presented. The design is based on the modulation of the optical signal in a plasmonic slot waveguide by the nonlinearity induced from the electro-optic polymer. The slot between two gold electrodes is coated with an EO polymer with a relatively large pockels coefficient and the voltage is applied to the gold electrodes. The total length of the structure is 100μm. Simulation is performed by the FEM and FDTD method and it is shown that the half wave voltage of V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</sub>=0.7 can be achieved for slot width of 100nm with a propagation loss of 0.955 dB/μm. By increasing the slot width to 140nm, V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</sub>=1.512V and Loss=6305.8dB/cm are obtained.

articleTitle: Robust decentralized networked control design for multi-area load frequency control
abstract: In this paper, a robust decentralized feedback control is proposed for large scale networked control systems. Some less conservative sufficient conditions are presented for existence of the robust decentralized feedback controller for large scale networked control system under digital communication to have maximum robustness against admissible time delays, consecutive packet loss, disturbances and interactions between the subsystems. The validity of the proposed method is illustrated by applying it to a load-frequency control problem for a multi-area power system with digital communication. Simulation results show more robustness and performance improvement of the proposed method in comparison with conventional methods.

articleTitle: The asymptotic secrecy rate of decentralized wireless networks
abstract: This paper studies the achievable secrecy rate of a decentralized wireless network consisting of N communication links exchanging information over a shared channel. It is assumed that there are M eavesdroppers attempting to listen to the transmitted information. In this regard, an on-off strategy is proposed to maximize the achievable secrecy rate of such network. Accordingly, it is shown that for large values of N, when the number of eavesdroppers (M) is less than N/(log n)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the achievable sum secrecy-rate scales as log 2N/M−2log log N+O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>(log(N).log log(N))/(log N)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Formulating multilateral trade-off of sensing, missed idle and transmission times in dynamic spectrum access networks
abstract: Many studies have been done in cognitive radios to maximize the network efficiency. The efficiency is usually defined in the form of throughput, energy efficiency or spectrum efficiency. With the advent of dynamic spectrum access concept in wireless networks, efficiency in such networks must be defined in order to best consider all the important metrics involved. For example, many works in cognitive radio network (CRN) neglect the interference due to primary user returns to the frequency band, and moreover; nobody has considered missed idle times during waiting throughout the entire current frame when the channel is sensed busy at the beginning. Both mentioned interference and missed opportunities depend on primary user traffic characteristics, secondary network communication protocol, sensing time and transmission time. Clearly, to consider them, we define and formulate a new efficiency metric in network dynamic access strategy called Access Efficiency in order to consider both interference, sensing time and missed opportunities due to transmission and waiting times respectively. Then, the optimized values for sensing and transmission time are computed using genetic algorithm in order to maximize Access Efficiency. The optimization point concurrently reduces missed idle times and maximizes successful transmission times (conventional throughput). It is obvious that a network protocol with higher Access Efficiency misses less idle times and imposes less collision on users.

articleTitle: Optimal participation of a wind power producer in a transmission-constrained electricity market
abstract: Wind generation is clean and cheap. However it forces the independent system operator to buy more reserves in order to maintain system security in a specified level. Therefore, two different forces exist to determine the optimal amount of wind power in the market. One of them is the low marginal cost of wind producers and another one is reserve increase which can raise the market price. The paper adopts linear programing to find the optimal amount of wind, considering transmission constraints, ramp-rate constraints of conventional generators and reserves. The analyses are considered to be from the system operator's view point. Finally, optimal participation of producers are calculated and discussed for IEEE 30-bus system.

articleTitle: Robust control of a magnetic levitation plant based on gap metric and stability margin
abstract: This paper focuses on integrating performance and stability to design a global controller based on multi-model technique. Gap metric is employed as a powerful tool to measure the distance between local linear models. The number of local models increases when they have inherently a small maximum stability margin. To overcome this problem, an improvement procedure is proposed that ensures avoiding redundancy issue. Also, stability and performance are incorporated to select the local nominal models. To evaluate the proposed method, a magnetic levitation plant which is a highly nonlinear system with unstable local models is studied. The efficiency of the proposed approach in set-point tracking and disturbance rejection is demonstrated in the simulations.

articleTitle: Comparison of ECG fiducial point extraction methods based on dynamic Bayesian network
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are one of the major causes of mortality in humans. One way to diagnose heart diseases and abnormalities is processing of cardiac signals such as electrocardiogram (ECG) signal. In many ECG analysis, location of peak, onset and offset of ECG waves must be extracted as a preprocessing step. These points are called ECG fiducial points (FPs) and convey clinically useful information. In this paper, we compare some FP extraction methods including three methods proposed recently by our research team. These methods are based on extended Kalman filter (EKF), hidden Markov model (HMM) and switching Kalman filter (SKF). Results are given for ECG signals of QT database. For all proposed methods, the mean of estimation error across all FPs are less than 4 msec (one sample) and their root mean square error are less than 17 msec (almost 4 samples). The proposed methods are also compared with two other methods based on wavelet transform and partially collapsed Gibbs sampler (PCGS). The obtained results by proposed methods outperform two other methods.

articleTitle: Optimal power allocation for distributed MIMO C-RAN system with limited fronthaul capacity
abstract: This paper investigates the optimal power allocation for the downlink of Multiple-Input Multiple Output (MIMO) Cloud Radio Access Networks (C-RAN) with limited fronthaul capacity in terms of maximizing Energy Efficiency (EE). In the considered system, the compressed and precoded message generated by Central Unit (CU) is transmitted to Remote Radio Heads (RRHs) via a fronthaul link with limited capacity, and the RRHs and Users Equipments (UEs) are assumed to be clustered into S cluster set. Here, we used an iterative algorithm with Lagrangian function to optimize the EE.

articleTitle: An integrated performance and robust stability based multi-model control of nonlinear systems: A pH neutralization reactor
abstract: This paper presents a new multi-model control scheme which integrates the stability and performance requirements to determine the nominal local models. Gap metric and stability margin concepts are applied to measure the distance between the local models and to grid the operation range of nonlinear system, respectively. The minimization of the integral of time absolute error is included as performance criterion. Furthermore, the multi-model decomposition and local controllers design are integrated in an optimization problem which provides avoidance of the redundancy issue. A fixed PI structure is considered as the local controllers to simplify the global multi-model controller structure. Therefore, the advantages of the presented method are: to avoid the dependency on experience, to eliminate the redundancy problem, to guarantee the stability and performance, and to have a simple structure. A pH neutralization reactor is simulated to evaluate the efficiency of the proposed method. Results demonstrate that this approach is systematic and works better than the traditional multi-model controller in terms of set-point tracking and disturbance rejection.

articleTitle: A highly-linear transconductor for Gm-C tracking filters employed in digital TV tuners
abstract: In this paper, a highly-linear CMOS transconductor for use in tracking low-pass G<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>-C filters employed in digital TV tuners is proposed. In order to improve the linearity of the proposed transconductor at the wide VHF/UHF frequency bands, a new linearization technique based on parallel operation of auxiliary transconductors in triode and subthreshold regions is proposed. Based on the proposed transconductor, a third-order elliptic low-pass G<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>-C filter is designed and simulated in a standard 0.18-μm CMOS technology. The cutoff frequency of the filter is tunable from 50MHz to 300 MHz.
